title: Validity of Estimating the Maximal Oxygen Consumption by Consumer Wearables: A Systematic Review with Meta-analysis and Expert Statement of the INTERLIVE Network
authors: Molina-Garcia P, Notbohm HL, Schumann M, Argent R, Hetherington-Rauth M, Stang J, et al.
population: Validation studies of wearable-estimated VO2max (14 studies)
findings: Wearables using resting-condition information significantly overestimated VO2max (bias 2.17 ml/kg/min; limits of agreement -13.07 to 17.41).
Devices using exercise-based algorithms had lower error (bias -0.09 ml/kg/min; limits of agreement -9.92 to 9.74).

Authors conclude exercise-based estimation seems optimal at population level but individual-level error is large, so for sport or clinical use it needs improvement; an INTERLIVE statement proposes six validation domains.
limitations: Only 14 heterogeneous studies; no brand- or running-specific results in the abstract. Crossref lists a 2026 correction (10.1007/s40279-026-02547-9), contents not checked.
implications: Treat watch VO2max or fitness scores as noisy (about plus or minus 10 ml/kg/min individual limits of agreement); do not derive training paces from them.
Set zones from the athlete's own hard efforts and race results; use device VO2max only as a smoothed trend.

verification.notes: Crossref: title, Sports Med, 2022-01-24, first author Molina-Garcia match. PubMed/Europe PMC abstract re-read; added resting-based bias/LoA numbers. Erratum claim verified as a Crossref 'Correction' relation dated 2026-10-13.
